title: Lunch on points
setting: Saturday lunchtime in town. Mai and Sora, who know each other through Yuki and Kenta, have spent the morning shopping together. Sora's hands are full of bags; Mai hasn't bought a thing. They stop outside a small ramen shop Sora likes.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sora-kun, ippai katta ne. kyou, kekkou okane tsukatta n ja nai?
lines.ja: ソラくん、いっぱい買ったね。今日、結構お金使ったんじゃない？
lines.kana: そらくん、いっぱいかったね。きょう、けっこうおかねつかったんじゃない？
lines.english: Sora, you bought loads. You've spent quite a bit of money today, haven't you?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: un, kongetsu mou okane tsukaisugichatta. demo itsumo kaado tsukatte, pointo tameteru kara ii n da.
lines.ja: うん、今月もうお金使いすぎちゃった。でもいつもカード使って、ポイント貯めてるからいいんだ。
lines.kana: うん、こんげつもうおかねつかいすぎちゃった。でもいつもカードつかって、ポイントためてるからいいんだ。
lines.english: Yeah, I've already spent too much this month. But it's fine, because I always pay by card and collect the points.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e, sore tte, pointo wa tameteru kedo, okane wa tamete nai jan.
lines.ja: え、それって、ポイントは貯めてるけど、お金は貯めてないじゃん。
lines.kana: え、それって、ポイントはためてるけど、おかねはためてないじゃん。
lines.english: Wait, so you're collecting points, but you're not saving any money.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: datte, kaado da to, okane tsukatteru kanji shinai n da yo ne.
lines.ja: だって、カードだと、お金使ってる感じしないんだよね。
lines.kana: だって、カードだと、おかねつかってるかんじしないんだよね。
lines.english: Well, when it's a card, it doesn't feel like I'm spending money.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sore ga abunai n da yo. watashi wa ima, ryokou no okane tameteru n da.
lines.ja: それが危ないんだよ。私は今、旅行のお金貯めてるんだ。
lines.kana: それがあぶないんだよ。わたしはいま、りょこうのおかねためてるんだ。
lines.english: That's exactly the danger. Me, I'm saving up for a trip right now.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: e, ryokou? doko ni iku no?
lines.kana: え、りょこう？どこにいくの？
lines.english: Oh, a trip? Where are you going?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: mada kimete nai kedo, rainen, hitori de ryokou ni ikitai n da.
lines.ja: まだ決めてないけど、来年、一人で旅行に行きたいんだ。
lines.kana: まだきめてないけど、らいねん、ひとりでりょこうにいきたいんだ。
lines.english: I haven't decided yet, but next year I want to go travelling on my own.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: hitori de? sugoi naa. boku mo okane tamenakya.
lines.ja: 一人で？すごいなあ。僕もお金貯めなきゃ。
lines.kana: ひとりで？すごいなあ。ぼくもおかねためなきゃ。
lines.english: On your own? That's amazing. I need to start saving money too.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: a, mou ichiji da. onaka suita ne.
lines.ja: あ、もう一時だ。おなかすいたね。
lines.kana: あ、もういちじだ。おなかすいたね。
lines.english: Oh, it's already one o'clock. I'm hungry, aren't you?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: kono mise no raamen, oishii n da yo. a, demo koko, kaado tsukaeru kana?
lines.ja: この店のラーメン、おいしいんだよ。あ、でもここ、カード使えるかな？
lines.kana: このみせのラーメン、おいしいんだよ。あ、でもここ、カードつかえるかな？
lines.english: The ramen here is really good. Oh, but I wonder if I can pay by card here.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: uun, koko wa genkin dake da yo. kono aida kita kedo, kaado tsukaenakatta.
lines.ja: ううん、ここは現金だけだよ。この間来たけど、カード使えなかった。
lines.kana: ううん、ここはげんきんだけだよ。このあいだきたけど、カードつかえなかった。
lines.english: No, it's cash only. I came the other day and couldn't pay by card.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: e, uso! genkin, sanbyaku en shika nai.
lines.ja: え、うそ！現金、三百円しかない。
lines.kana: え、うそ！げんきん、さんびゃくえんしかない。
lines.english: No way! I've only got three hundred yen in cash.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: jaa, asoko no konbini ni shiyou. konbini nara kaado tsukaeru shi.
lines.ja: じゃあ、あそこのコンビニにしよう。コンビニならカード使えるし。
lines.kana: じゃあ、あそこのコンビニにしよう。コンビニならカードつかえるし。
lines.english: Then let's go to that konbini over there instead. You can pay by card at a konbini.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: sou da! kyou no gohan wa, boku ga ogoru yo. tameta pointo de.
lines.ja: そうだ！今日のご飯は、僕がおごるよ。貯めたポイントで。
lines.kana: そうだ！きょうのごはんは、ぼくがおごるよ。ためたポイントで。
lines.english: I know! Lunch is on me today. With the points I've collected.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e, ii no? pointo, sonna ni aru no?
lines.ja: え、いいの？ポイント、そんなにあるの？
lines.kana: え、いいの？ポイント、そんなにあるの？
lines.english: Really? Have you got that many points?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: un, sanzen pointo aru yo. hora, pointo tameru no mo daiji desho?
lines.ja: うん、三千ポイントあるよ。ほら、ポイント貯めるのも大事でしょ？
lines.kana: うん、さんぜんポイントあるよ。ほら、ポイントためるのもだいじでしょ？
lines.english: Yep, three thousand. See? Collecting points matters too, right?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: hai hai, arigatou. demo raigetsu wa, okane mo tamete ne.
lines.ja: はいはい、ありがとう。でも来月は、お金も貯めてね。
lines.kana: はいはい、ありがとう。でもらいげつは、おかねもためてね。
lines.english: Yeah, yeah, thank you. But next month, save some money too, OK?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: wakatta. raigetsu wa kaado tsukawanai yo. tabun.
lines.ja: わかった。来月はカード使わないよ。たぶん。
lines.kana: わかった。らいげつはカードつかわないよ。たぶん。
lines.english: Got it. Next month I won't use my card. Probably.

choices.english: Mai lends Sora some of her trip savings so they can eat ramen.
Sora decides to stop paying by card and pays for the ramen in cash.
The ramen shop is cash only, so they go to a konbini, and Sora treats Mai with his points.

questions.explanation: Lines 10-12: Sora wonders if the ramen shop takes cards, Mai says it's cash only, and Sora has just 300 yen on him. Line 13: Mai suggests the konbini, where cards work. Line 14: Sora says lunch is on him, paid with the points he has collected (tameta pointo de). A is wrong because Mai is saving for her trip (line 5) and never lends him anything. B is wrong because Sora only says he won't use his card next month, and adds tabun, 'probably' (line 18); with 300 yen he couldn't pay for ramen anyway.

questions.english: You've spent the day shopping with Yuki and bought far more than you meant to. She says: "Today's shopping was fun! Let's go again." Agree, but say you spent too much money.
questions.ja: 今日の買い物、楽しかったね！また行こうよ。
questions.kana: きょうのかいもの、たのしかったね！またいこうよ。
questions.romaji: kyou no kaimono, tanoshikatta ne! mata ikou yo.
questions.answer: Say you overspent with okane o tsukau plus -sugiru: tanoshikatta kedo, okane tsukaisugichatta. Not sugosu, which is only for time.

modelAnswers.ja: うん、楽しかった！でも、お金使いすぎちゃった。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, it was fun! But I spent way too much money.

modelAnswers.romaji: tanoshikatta kedo, kongetsu wa mou okane tsukaenai yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 楽しかったけど、今月はもうお金使えないよ。
modelAnswers.english: It was fun, but I can't spend any more money this month.

questions.explanation: Spending money is tsukau, 'use': Mai asks kyou, kekkou okane tsukatta n ja nai? (line 1), and Sora admits kongetsu mou okane tsukaisugichatta (line 2). The dictionary words for 'spend' don't fit here: sugosu is only for time (shuumatsu o sugosu, spend the weekend), and tsuiyasu sounds like a written report. -sugichatta adds 'too much, oops'.

questions.english: Outside the ramen shop, what does Sora wonder?
questions.ja: 店の前で、ソラくんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: みせのまえで、そらくんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: mise no mae de, sora-kun wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Do they take cards here, I wonder?
I wonder if I can pay by card here.
I wonder if they accept cards here.

questions.explanation: Line 10: a, demo koko, kaado tsukaeru kana? Asking whether a place takes cards uses tsukau in its can-form: 'can I use a card here?'. Mai answers the same way: kaado tsukaenakatta (line 11) and konbini nara kaado tsukaeru shi (line 13). A is 'take' word for word, but toru means picking something up or taking it away, not accepting a payment. C is 'accept' word for word; ukeru is for things like taking an exam or a phone call, and kaado ukeru doesn't ask about paying.

questions.english: Kenta has noticed you keep skipping nights out and asks: "You never come out drinking lately. Are you busy?" Tell him you're saving up money right now.
questions.ja: 最近、飲みに来ないね。忙しいの？
questions.kana: さいきん、のみにこないね。いそがしいの？
questions.romaji: saikin, nomi ni konai ne. isogashii no?
questions.answer: Say you're saving up with tameru in the -teru form: uun, ima okane tameteru n da. Not hozon suru, which is saving a file.

modelAnswers.romaji: uun, ima okane tameteru n da.
modelAnswers.ja: ううん、今お金貯めてるんだ。
modelAnswers.english: No, I'm saving up money right now.

modelAnswers.romaji: isogashiku nai kedo, ima ryokou no okane tameteru kara, gomen ne.
modelAnswers.ja: 忙しくないけど、今旅行のお金貯めてるから、ごめんね。
modelAnswers.english: I'm not busy, but I'm saving up for a trip right now, so sorry.

questions.explanation: Saving up is tameru, 'let it pile up', usually as tameteru while you're still at it: Mai says ima, ryokou no okane tameteru n da (line 5), and Sora says boku mo okane tamenakya (line 8). English 'save' leads elsewhere: hozon suru is saving a file, tasukeru is saving a person, and setsuyaku is cutting back. chokin shiteru also works.

questions.english: Sora says he always pays by card and collects the points. What does Mai point out about that?
questions.ja: マイさんはソラくんのポイントについて、何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: まいさんはそらくんのポイントについて、なんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: mai-san wa sora-kun no pointo ni tsuite, nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: His points are piling up, but he isn't saving any money.
He's using up his points as fast as his money.
He's saving money by paying with points instead of cash.

questions.explanation: Line 3: pointo wa tameteru kedo, okane wa tamete nai jan. The same verb tameru does both jobs: collecting points (pointo tameteru, line 2) and saving money (okane tameteru, line 5), and Mai's wa ... wa sets the two against each other: one is piling up, the other isn't. B mixes tameru up with tsukau, spending. C turns it around: Sora pays by card, and only spends his points at the very end, at the konbini (tameta pointo de, line 14).

newWords.english: too much (tsukaisugichatta = I spent too much)
